title: Trace bookmarking and widget ownership playbook
body:
Purpose:
This doc proposes a lightweight, pragmatic approach for 'trace bookmarking' (operator-driven bookmarks that mark traces as important) and for assigning clear widget ownership on dashboards. Goal: make investigations faster, reduce finger-pointing, and keep dashboard drift under control without adding heavy process overhead.

Background / motivation:
- We have a large set of runtime widgets and ~3x more ad-hoc trace captures than we can meaningfully review. Operators often leave scratch notes in Slack threads; those disappear.
- Investigations are slowed by: unclear widget owners, no canonical way to mark interesting traces for follow-up, and dashboards that silently change without an audit trail.
- This playbook is intended to be a low-friction set of conventions and a tiny instrumented API for bookmarks, not a full-change governance model.

Key definitions (shorthand used below):
- bookmark: a short metadata tag attached to a trace at capture time (or marked post-capture) indicating it needs follow-up. Lightweight: reason tag + owner + ticket optional.
- anchor span: the span within a trace that represents the user-visible request boundary (e.g., api.request -> model.encode). Bookmarks should reference anchor spans for stable navigation.
- widget owner: the primary engineer or team responsible for a dashboard widget's correctness, queries, and alert thresholds.
- steward: a role that manages cross-widget hygiene, periodic audits, and onboarding docs. Typically eng-observability.

Principles:
- low ceremony: bookmarks are quick (1-2 clicks or a small API call).
- discoverability: bookmarks must surface in dashboards and investigation UIs (searchable).
- ownership over policing: widget owners are empowered but steward coordinates audits.
- iterative: start with minimal signals and tighten processes as needed.

Instrumentation patterns (how bookmarks get created):
- Operator UI (preferred): the investigation UI shows a "Bookmark" button that opens a small form (reason: free text, severity: triage/urgent, owner: autocompleted). This writes a tag to the trace storage and creates a lightweight record in the bookmarks index.
- SDK API: telemetry.bookmark(trace_id, reason, owner_email?, ticket?) for programmatic marking (used by scripts or automated checks).
- Post-capture tagging: allow marking traces after the fact from a trace viewer; the viewer must validate anchor span linkage so later drilldowns map correctly.

Bookmark schema (minimal):
- trace_id (required)
body_continued:
- anchor_span_id (recommended)
- reason (short free text)
- severity (triage | action | info)
- owner (email)
- created_by (email)
- ticket (optional)
- created_at
- status (open | acknowledged | resolved)

Sampling and capture rules (practical guidance):
- We cannot keep full traces for everything. Two-tier approach:
  1) auto-capture: retain short-span traces for p95/p99 latency outliers and error responses (keep for 7 days).
  2) bookmark-capture: when a bookmark is created for a sample not already fully instrumented, trigger an on-demand extended capture (retain for 30 days, full KV/headers).
- Sampling heuristics: use adaptive sampling that increases sample rate for endpoints with recent bookmarks or rising error signals.
- Budgeting: define a weekly trace budget per region; once budget approaches, reduce background sample retention by lowering sample rate for low-priority routes.

Bookmarking heuristics (how operators should decide to bookmark):
- Bookmark if: there is an actionable root cause candidate, recurring errors with unclear origin, or an SLO breach with unknown driver.
- Do not bookmark: transient downstream flakiness where a vendor ticket will be opened immediately and responsibility is clear (instead update the vendor ticket).
- Use short reasons ("kv-cache-miss spike", "quantize-fallback-regen", "routing: dedicated->host fallback") to aid quick searching.

Widget ownership model and lightweight SLAs:
- Each dashboard widget card MUST have a metadata panel with: owner, last updated (YYYY-MM-DD), data source, instrumented spans/tags, and a quality note with known caveats.
- Owners are expected to: respond to paging/mentions within 48 hours, accept or reassign bookmarks related to their widget, and attend quarterly dashboard audits.
- Steward team runs monthly lightweight audits where they pick 10% of widgets with highest edit rates and verify owner contact info and instrumentation links.

Widget lifecycle checklist (owner must fill in these fields on creation or major edit):
- statement of intent (1-2 lines)
- expected users and runbook link
- metric definition and source query
- anchor spans or event keys used for trace joins
- alert thresholds and rationale
- retention and expected query cost
- test query and sample trace id for verification

Investigation flow (example):
1) Alert fires for p99 latency spike. Ops opens trace view -> finds several traces -> bookmarks two traces (reason + owner set to "model-serving team").
2) Bookmark creates quick ticket (optional) and notifies owner by email/Slack with trace links.
3) Owner acknowledges within 48h, updates bookmark status, and attaches RCA to ticket.
4) If fix requires dashboard changes, owner updates widget and increments widget version metadata.

Operational UIs and telemetry surfaces:
- Bookmark index: a searchable table (filters: owner, status, severity, tag, date) with direct trace links and anchor span preview.
- Dashboard ribbon: show recent bookmarks affecting widgets (n=5) and quick link to bookmark index.
- On-call console integration: when looking at an alert, show any open bookmarks in the last 72h for relevant routes.

Audit and clean-up policy:
- Open bookmarks older than 90 days require steward review and will be auto-closed as 'stale' if no owner action.
- Widgets without an owner for >60 days are flagged and steward will assign a temporary owner.
- Quarterly: export bookmark metadata to a CSV for retention and near-term analysis of investigation load.

Minimal implementation milestones (MVP):
- M1 (2 weeks): lightweight bookmark API + UI button + searchable index that stores the minimal schema.
- M2 (4 weeks): dashboard metadata panel + owner field + simple audit job that flags unowned widgets.
- M3 (8 weeks): adaptive sampling hookup so bookmarks can trigger extended capture; integrate notifications into on-call flows.

Open questions / unresolved trade-offs:
- Should bookmarks be immutable after creation (we currently allow status/owner updates). Immutability improves auditability but hurts operator ergonomics.
- How to balance trace budget vs. investigations during major incidents? Proposed: temporarily lift region budgets via an incident toggle owned by SRE.
- Instrumentation backward-compat: how many older widgets lack anchor spans? We need a find-and-tag migration script.

Action items (owners):
- Jesse: prototype bookmark API + small UI button (P0) — JIRA-OBS-4823.
- Noah: dashboard metadata panel prototype + widget-owner column (P1).
- Amira: stewarding checklist + audit job definition; coordinate first audit in 6 weeks.
- Lina: add bookmark index search filters and link to on-call console.

References and links:
- Trace sampling playbook (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Sampling+Playbook
- Telemetry PR for soft-delete and retention: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/214

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep initial schema tiny. Resist the urge to model everything.
- We want bookmarks to be the one small durable signal that survives Slack threads and ephemeral notes.
- Follow up: check storage cost estimates for on-demand full capture (Noah to run numbers).

This is a working draft — feedback welcome.
